issues.description: Class name mismatch for the concrete Animal types: the problem statement (UML and tasks) and the template Main.java refer to concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat. In the solution repository the concrete implementations are instead named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (classes declared at src/de/tum/cit/ase/SpaceSeal.java:4, SpacePig.java:3, SpaceGoat.java:3), while the files Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution are empty. This inconsistency breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the exercise description/template and the provided solution artifacts and can cause confusion or test/compilation failures when code or tests reference Seal/Pig/Goat by those exact names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make class names consistent between the problem/template and the solution. Either (A) rename the solution classes SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, Goat (updating their source filenames and any internal references) so the expected identifiers exist, or (B) add small wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, Goat that delegate to the existing Space* implementations and provide the same public constructors and methods described in the UML. Ensure the public API (constructors, implemented interfaces, and messageOnFeed/messageOnRide/messageOnMilk method signatures and behaviors) matches the exercise description so students and tests can refer to Seal/Pig/Goat unambiguously.
